correctnessFindings.assessment: CDP responses and debugger notifications share the existing outbound queue, retaining message ordering and response/session associations. WeakMap ownership and close cleanup prevent an old connection from keeping a queue alive.
The reused defaults are 8 MiB soft native buffering, 64 MiB hard queued bytes, 4096 queued frames, 25 ms polling, and 128 frames per drain turn. On overflow, this caller terminates the CDP client.

maxFrameBytes=Infinity preserves direct delivery of an individual large screenshot/PDF response on a draining connection. JSON serialization and a single direct-send frame can still allocate beyond the queue budget.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: Ordinary CDP automation sees the same messages. A client that cannot read fast enough now disconnects once queued bytes or frame count overflow; outstanding commands and notifications may be lost and require caller recovery.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: This introduces a finite CDP backlog with connection termination on overflow. Reconnection is not a guarantee of command/event replay, and no automatic replay protocol is added.

platformEvidence.assessment: Queue and WebSocket logic is JavaScript without a changed native process or path contract. Fresh writer tests ran on macOS. This does not establish real browser automation behavior under native Windows/Linux network stalls.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.

originalReview.sshAndFolderCases: Local and forwarded CDP sockets retain their existing routing. Slow SSH forwarding can trigger the same overload disconnect. No workspace type or process liveness inference is introduced.

regressionCoverage.description: The fresh batch includes cdp-client-response-writer.test.ts. Source review also follows debugger notifications into the writer and the shared queue default limits and overflow callback.
